CORE DESIGN VALUES

How to Nathan

The standards I bring to my code, interfaces, documentation, and design process.

01 · Documentation and understanding

I want my code to communicate its intent. Clear naming, readable structure, and documentation should help someone follow what a program does and why it works that way. The standard I chase goes beyond familiarity with a language: if someone who does not know that language can still understand the logic and purpose of my code, I have gone beyond the baseline I set for myself.

02 · The black box approach

I design methods, interfaces, and programs to work correctly and to be usable without requiring a complete understanding of their implementation. A developer should be able to understand the parameters, where the inputs come from, how they are used, and what the return values mean. Clear interfaces and documentation make that possible. Someone using a tool should be able to learn how to use it without first learning how it was built.

03 · Organization is efficiency

I approach everything I design and implement with a consistent format and organization in mind. I use GitHub to keep my work available between my desktop and laptop, and to make classwork and examples easy to share with others. I also use UML and visual design to work through code structure and relationships. Planning how the pieces fit together helps me understand a system before and while I build it.

Nathan Ng / Understanding creates capability. Capability creates new questions.
